java: ClassDiagramFactory registers CommandCreateClass before CommandPackageWithUSymbol and before the later deployment factory path, so a full source accepted by class commands remains a class diagram.

CommandCreateClass accepts TYPE=(interface|enum|annotation|abstract class|class|entity|circle|diamond|protocol|struct|exception|metaclass|stereotype|dataclass|record|map); interface-only class syntax is not excluded from the class factory.
rust: detect_uml_subtype only suppresses quoted-container deployment promotion when has_non_interface_class_decl is true.
Quoted node/cloud/database containers are still treated as deployment signals when only interface declarations are present, even though interface declarations are valid class-factory inputs in Java.
source_inspection.fixture_shaping_search: No mechanism-name string or held-out filename was found in shipping crate logic; only unit-test strings reference the implementer's example labels.

perturbations.evidence: Java emits data-diagram-type=CLASS. Rust emits data-diagram-type=DESCRIPTION and serializes Host as an entity rather than a cluster.
Java emits a CLASS diagram with an Outer package cluster and nested cloud cluster. Rust emits DESCRIPTION with a different element count (16 vs 27) and different cluster/entity shapes.
The supported non-interface-class case compares cleanly, so the counterexamples isolate the interface-only guard rather than a general parser collapse.

findings: Reject: the mechanism claim is incomplete because Java's class factory accepts interface declarations through CommandCreateClass, but Rust only suppresses quoted-container deployment promotion for has_non_interface_class_decl.
Fresh valid held-outs with quoted node and quoted cloud containers plus interface-only class syntax both render as Java CLASS SVGs but Rust DESCRIPTION SVGs.
No fixture-shaped branch was found in shipping crate logic; this is a model mismatch in subtype detection, not a checker-input special case.
